output.title: Why do database indexes make queries faster, and what do they cost?
output.summary: Without an index, finding rows that match a condition means a sequential scan: reading every row of the table.

scenes.goal: Explain index is a separate sorted structure
scenes.narration: Let us walk through computer science fundamentals one step at a time. An index is a separate data structure, most commonly a B-tree, that keeps the values of one or more columns in sorted order with pointers to the rows, so the database can find a value in logarithmic time and read only the matching rows.
